statements: SELECT c.relname, i.indisvalid, i.indisready FROM pg_index i JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = i.indexrelid JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname = COALESCE(NULLIF(%s, ''), current_schema()) AND c.relname IN ('source_evidence_dedupe_lookup_idx', 'source_evidence_object_id_lookup_idx')
DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS "source_ingest"."source_evidence_dedupe_lookup_idx" (only when pg_index shows indisvalid=false or indisready=false from an interrupted earlier build)
DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS "source_ingest"."source_evidence_object_id_lookup_idx" (only when pg_index shows indisvalid=false or indisready=false from an interrupted earlier build)

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS source_evidence_dedupe_lookup_idx ON source_ingest.source_evidence (record_type, (CASE record_type WHEN 'source_record' THEN payload->'metadata'->>'source_dedupe_key' WHEN 'evidence_item' THEN payload->'metadata'->>'evidence_dedupe_key' END), append_id DESC, COALESCE(payload->'metadata'->>'tenant_id', ''))

CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS source_evidence_object_id_lookup_idx ON source_ingest.source_evidence (record_type, (CASE record_type WHEN 'source_record' THEN payload->>'source_id' WHEN 'evidence_item' THEN payload->>'evidence_item_id' WHEN 'evidence_bundle' THEN payload->>'evidence_bundle_id' WHEN 'knowledge_object' THEN payload->>'knowledge_object_id' END), append_id DESC)
acceptance_4_safe_hosted_schema_change.why_non_blocking: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS runs on the autocommit=True psycopg connection and acquires only a SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE lock on source_ingest.source_evidence rather than SHARE (standard CREATE INDEX) or ACCESS EXCLUSIVE (ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN ... STORED). SHARE UPDATE EXCLUSIVE does not conflict with ROW EXCLUSIVE locks taken by concurrent INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE writes or ACCESS SHARE locks taken by concurrent readers, so the service writer is not blocked during the index build on the 203 MB table.
acceptance_4_safe_hosted_schema_change.invalid_index_detection_and_repair: If a previous CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY build was interrupted (process killed or connection lost during one of the ~17 source-ingest container recreations per Taiwan refresh), PostgreSQL leaves an index entry with indisvalid = false (or indisready = false) that the planner never uses and that a bare CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS would skip forever. At bootstrap, _ensure_concurrent_lookup_indexes checks pg_index.indisvalid and pg_index.indisready for both source_evidence_dedupe_lookup_idx and source_evidence_object_id_lookup_idx; if either index exists with not (indisvalid and indisready), it logs a warning, drops the broken index with DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS, logs the rebuild, and recreates it with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS. Verified on real Postgres in test_bootstrap_repairs_invalid_concurrent_lookup_indexes_and_explain_uses_repaired_indexes.
acceptance_4_safe_hosted_schema_change.concurrent_bootstrap_two_processes_behav: When two processes bootstrap at the same time (for example the long-running API container and a scheduler or one-shot container), _bootstrap serializes schema/index initialization per table using a session-level PostgreSQL advisory lock acquired by polling SELECT pg_try_advisory_lock(hashtext('source_ingest.source_evidence.bootstrap'), hashtext(self.table)) on the autocommit=True connection and released in finally via pg_advisory_unlock. Because each pg_try_advisory_lock call completes immediately in autocommit mode, the waiting process holds no open virtual transaction or snapshot while sleeping between polls, so the lock holder's DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY / CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY phases complete without virtual-transaction deadlock. Once the first process finishes building (or repairing) the indexes and releases the advisory lock, the second process acquires the lock, queries pg_index, sees both source_evidence_dedupe_lookup_idx and source_evidence_object_id_lookup_idx already exist with indisvalid=true and indisready=true, logs that they are already valid and ready, and returns immediately: no error and no duplicate build. If the first process is killed or disconnects mid-build, PostgreSQL automatically releases its session advisory lock on disconnect and the second process detects not (indisvalid and indisready), drops the invalid index with DROP INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF EXISTS, and rebuilds it cleanly. Verified on real Postgres in test_two_processes_bootstrapping_concurrently_succeed_without_error_or_duplicate_build.
acceptance_4_safe_hosted_schema_change.rollback_reader_compatibility: Verified in test_startup_concurrent_index_ddl_and_rollback_reader_compatibility: no table columns or constraints are removed or altered, and the previous release's SELECT and INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (record_type, record_id) DO UPDATE queries operate identically with the new expression indexes present.

acceptance_7_runtime_budget.writer_kind: PostgreSQL B-tree expression indexes on source_ingest.source_evidence (source_evidence_dedupe_lookup_idx and source_evidence_object_id_lookup_idx)
acceptance_7_runtime_budget.cadence: Created idempotently once at service startup via CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY IF NOT EXISTS; maintained synchronously by PostgreSQL on each source_evidence INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (record_type, record_id) DO UPDATE during ingest runs
acceptance_7_runtime_budget.growth_per_day_at_current_ingest_rate: At the current hosted ingest rate (~1,500-4,000 net new source_evidence rows/day across scheduled non-collector profiles and collector bundle summaries; re-ingested existing dedupe keys update in place via ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE with 0 net row growth), combined index growth is approximately 0.28-0.75 MiB/day (~193 bytes/new row).
acceptance_7_runtime_budget.cap_and_cleanup: Bounded by source_ingest.source_evidence table retention and in-place conflict upserts on (record_type, record_id); both indexes are table-owned PostgreSQL objects that are cleaned automatically on row deletion/vacuum and dropped automatically with the table (DROP TABLE / DROP SCHEMA CASCADE).
